# Standard CSV format

The standard format is Glovebox's own, fully documented CSV layout. Export it to move your data, or convert another app's export into it and import it with the **Glovebox** preset. Importing from another app directly is described in [Import](import.md); the export side is in [Export and backup](export.md).

A machine-readable description (a Data Package with one Table Schema per table) is available as [standard-format.datapackage.json](standard-format.datapackage.json). A full backup contains the same description as `datapackage.json`.

## Conventions

- **File:** RFC 4180 CSV. Comma delimiter, `"` quoting, CRLF line ends, one header row. UTF-8 without a byte order mark when written; a BOM is accepted when read.
- **Dates and times:** dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`, times `HH:MM` (`HH:MM:SS` is accepted when reading).
- **Numbers:** dot as decimal separator, no thousands separator.
- **Booleans:** `true` or `false`.
- **Empty cells:** an empty cell means no value. Columns that do not apply to a row's type stay empty.
- **Units:** distances in kilometres, volumes in litres, money as a decimal number in the currency named in `currency`. The unit is part of the column name where a column has one.
- **Currency:** a non-empty `currency` that differs from the app currency makes that row an error on import.
- **Precision on export:** `fuel_l` and `price_per_l` with 3 decimals, `total` with 2 decimals, `odometer_km` without trailing zeros.

### Rules per record type

- `type` is `refuel` or `expense`. `type`, `vehicle` and `date` are required on every row.
- A refuel needs `odometer_km` and two of `fuel_l`, `price_per_l` and `total`; the third is calculated.
- An expense needs `title` and a `total` greater than 0. `coverage_start` and `coverage_end` are set both or neither.
- Records refer to vehicles by name and to stations by name and location.

## Optional tables: vehicles and stations

`records.csv` alone is enough. To bring vehicle and station details along, put `vehicles.csv` and/or `stations.csv` next to `records.csv` in a ZIP file, or in a ZIP of several CSV files, and import the ZIP. The ZIP does not need a `datapackage.json`.

- A vehicle or station that does not exist yet is created with all the details given.
- A vehicle (matched by `name`) or station (matched by `name` and `location`) that already exists is only completed: empty details are filled and nothing is overwritten.
- The import preview lists which vehicles and stations will be created or filled before you confirm.
- `stations.csv` can list stations that have no refuels yet.
- A full backup is exactly this, plus `datapackage.json`: it is made on the export page and restored on the import page like any other ZIP.

## `records.csv`

Refuels and expenses. Used by every standard import and export.

| Column | Type | Unit | Required | Applies to | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | enum |  | always | both | Kind of record. One of `refuel`, `expense`. | `refuel` |
| `vehicle` | string |  | always | both | Vehicle name. | `Golf` |
| `date` | date |  | always | both | Date of the record, YYYY-MM-DD. | `2026-05-02` |
| `time` | time |  | no | refuel | Time of day, HH:MM (HH:MM:SS is also accepted). | `14:30` |
| `odometer_km` | number | `km` | refuel rows | both | Odometer reading. | `98000` |
| `odometer_estimated` | boolean |  | no | expense | Written by Glovebox: the expense odometer is the last known reading, not an entered one. Leave empty. Empty means `false`. | `false` |
| `fuel_l` | number | `l` | no | refuel | Fuel quantity. Give two of fuel_l, price_per_l and total; the third is derived. | `45.200` |
| `price_per_l` | number | `currency/l` | no | refuel | Price per litre. Give two of fuel_l, price_per_l and total; the third is derived. | `1.459` |
| `total` | number | `currency` | expense rows | both | Refuel total, or expense amount (greater than 0). Refuel: give two of fuel_l, price_per_l and total. Expense: required. | `65.95` |
| `currency` | string |  | no | both | ISO 4217 currency code; must equal the app currency when given. | `EUR` |
| `full` | boolean |  | no | refuel | The tank was filled completely. Empty means `true`. | `true` |
| `missed_previous` | boolean |  | no | refuel | A fill-up before this one was not recorded. Empty means `false`. | `false` |
| `station` | string |  | no | refuel | Station name. | `OMV Celje` |
| `station_location` | string |  | no | refuel | Station location; with the name it identifies the station. | `Celje` |
| `station_brand` | string |  | no | refuel | Station brand; used only when the station is created. | `OMV` |
| `category` | enum |  | no | expense | Expense category. One of `maintenance`, `insurance`, `registration`, `other`. Empty means `other`. | `maintenance` |
| `title` | string |  | expense rows | expense | Short label of the expense. | `Oil change` |
| `coverage_start` | date |  | no | expense | First day the expense covers (insurance, registration), YYYY-MM-DD. Set both coverage_start and coverage_end, or neither. | `2026-01-01` |
| `coverage_end` | date |  | no | expense | Last day the expense covers, YYYY-MM-DD. Set both coverage_start and coverage_end, or neither. | `2026-12-31` |
| `notes` | string |  | no | both | Free text. | `Winter tyres` |
| `derived` | enum |  | no | refuel | Written by Glovebox: which refuel figure was derived. Leave empty. One of `fuel_l`, `price_per_l`, `total`. | `total` |
| `source` | string |  | no | both | Written by Glovebox: where the record came from. Leave empty. | `manual` |
| `source_ref` | string |  | no | both | Written by Glovebox: the record's id in its source. Leave empty. | `1042` |

## `vehicles.csv`

Optional. Vehicle details; see [Optional tables](#optional-tables-vehicles-and-stations).

| Column | Type | Unit | Required | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | always | Vehicle name, as used in records.csv. | `Golf` |
| `make` | string |  | no | Manufacturer. | `Volkswagen` |
| `model` | string |  | no | Model. | `Golf VII` |
| `plate` | string |  | no | Registration plate. | `LJ AB-123` |
| `fuel_type` | string |  | no | Fuel type. | `Diesel` |
| `initial_odometer_km` | number | `km` | no | Odometer when tracking started. | `85000` |
| `archived` | boolean |  | no | The vehicle is archived. Empty means `false`. | `false` |
| `notes` | string |  | no | Free text. | `Company car` |

## `stations.csv`

Optional. Station details and stations without refuels; see [Optional tables](#optional-tables-vehicles-and-stations).

| Column | Type | Unit | Required | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | always | Station name. | `OMV Celje` |
| `location` | string |  | no | Station location. | `Celje` |
| `brand` | string |  | no | Station brand. | `OMV` |

## Example

One refuel and one expense (`records.csv`):

```csv
type,vehicle,date,time,odometer_km,odometer_estimated,fuel_l,price_per_l,total,currency,full,missed_previous,station,station_location,station_brand,category,title,coverage_start,coverage_end,notes,derived,source,source_ref
refuel,Golf,2026-05-02,14:30,98000,,45.200,1.459,65.95,EUR,true,false,OMV Celje,Celje,OMV,,,,,,,,
expense,Golf,2026-05-10,,98400,,,,180.00,EUR,,,,,,maintenance,Oil change,,,Winter tyres,,,
```

## Convert your own export

Any CSV that follows the tables above can be imported with the **Glovebox** preset. You only need the columns that are required for your rows.

### With a spreadsheet

1. Open your export in a spreadsheet program.
2. Add a `type` column filled with `refuel` (or `expense`) and a `vehicle` column with the vehicle name.
3. Rename or move columns so that the headers match the tables above. Delete columns you do not need.
4. Make sure dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` and numbers use a dot as the decimal separator, with no thousands separator.
5. Save as CSV (UTF-8, comma delimited) and import it with the **Glovebox** preset.

### With a script

This Python example uses only the standard `csv` module. Adjust the file name and the source column names to your export.

```python
import csv

with open("my-export.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as src, \
        open("records.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as dst:
    out = csv.DictWriter(dst, ["type", "vehicle", "date", "odometer_km", "fuel_l", "total"])
    out.writeheader()
    for row in csv.DictReader(src):
        out.writerow({
            "type": "refuel", "vehicle": "Golf",
            "date": row["Date"],               # must be YYYY-MM-DD
            "odometer_km": row["Odometer"],
            "fuel_l": row["Litres"].replace(",", "."),
            "total": row["Cost"].replace(",", "."),
        })
```

If your export needs only renamed columns or another date or number format, a custom preset is easier than conversion: see [Presets](presets.md).
